topic: Ten-node Memory Grove and functional second tier
currentUserGoal: Move past the zoomable tree shell by expanding the Memory catalog and giving the redesign more meaningful long-term progression.
workCompleted: Expanded PermanentUpgradeId and the Memory Grove from five to ten save-compatible functional memories.
Added Fast Touch, Ancient Resilience, Sprinkler Tuning, Distributed Roots, and Emergency Photosynthesis as one real second-tier upgrade for each current prototype lane.
Applied the new effects to manual recovery, base Scourge drain, Tiny Sprinkler healing, wound pressure, and Last Stand revival without adding upgrade scans to the run tick.
Moved Memory node branch styling, icon assets, normalized positions, impact copy, flavor, and short effect text into a shared MemoryTreeCatalog.

Converted the tree to a fixed 720x450 logical world fitted inside the existing masked zoom/pan viewport, with overview nodes reduced to icon plus name and full details retained in hover/detail presentation.
Reused five original-game skill icons for the new memories and kept all ten nodes accessible through the transparent DOM agent layer.
Added catalog coverage that requires every upgrade to have presentation data and rejects connector crossings between unrelated branches.
Updated the durable redesign and implementation-plan documents with the ten-node catalog, second-tier effects, fixed-world contract, and current prototype lane caveat.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 46 Vitest tests across four files, TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
Focused coverage includes the run spine, tree viewport, and new catalog geometry.
Desktop browser smoke at 1280x720 bought all ten memories in prerequisite order, left the expected 4 GT from a 260 GT test grant, and found no missing Memory icon resources.
Browser screenshots verified the ten-node overview, active connector paths, 180% zoom, hover callout, enlarged detail icon, and long Emergency Photosynthesis title containment.
Begin Next Run browser smoke preserved all ten memories, returned to one active root and a 1x1 field, applied Deeper Roots for 125 max HP, and kept run tools hidden at run start.
currentGitStatus: Expected after this handoff commit: clean worktree on codex/gameplay-update, three commits ahead of origin/codex/gameplay-update.
knownIssues: The five new costs and effect values are first-pass tuning and need hands-on pacing feedback rather than more speculative expansion.
The current prototype lanes are Touch, Vitality, Automation, Scourge, and Resolve; the broader long-term Field Growth and Friends branches remain unimplemented.
This browser runtime remained fixed at 1280x720 and rejected the local narrow-frame harness, so the previously passing 390x844 compact smoke was not rerun for this slice.
Tree zoom/pan remains session-only UI state by design.
nextRecommendedSteps: Playtest several natural runs and tune second-tier costs against actual GT earnings and perceived survival impact.
Add focused branch navigation or fit-to-selection once the third tier makes panning materially useful.
Design the next catalog tier around Field Growth and Friends only after the current ten-node economy feels earned.
Re-run the compact 390x844 Memory Grove screenshot when a resizable browser surface is available.
doNotRevert: Keep Memory identity and presentation in MemoryTreeCatalog instead of restoring scene switch statements or hardcoded five-node DOM labels.
Keep the fixed logical tree world fitted inside the existing masked zoom/pan viewport.
Keep overview nodes name-only; cost, prerequisites, effect, flavor, and enlarged icon belong in hover/detail presentation.
Keep base drain, wound pressure, sprinkler healing, and revive ratio derived once at run creation rather than scanning permanent upgrades every tick.
Every new run must still return to one tile at mastery rank 0 while permanent GT and Memory upgrades survive.
